text:
Utah never had to survive Edmonton's best hockey, because the Oilers didn't show it until the game was nearly gone. In the first period UTA out-chanced EDM 1.52 to 0.25 in expected goals, and Barrett Hayton's power-play wrist shot at 10:38 turned that edge into a 1-0 lead. Kailer Yamamoto also had a 28% look in the period that Devon Levi stopped.

The game was effectively settled in the second. Clayton Keller made it 2-0 on another power play at 11:57, and after Leon Draisaitl cut it to 2-1 at 13:54, Logan Cooley answered 23 seconds later with a tip-in for 3-1. UTA went 2 for 3 on the power play (1.16 expected goals) while EDM went 0 for 2 (0.14). Shakir Mukhamadullin's snap shot early in the third, a chance of under 1%, made it 3-2, and EDM held the better of the period (0.71 expected goals to 0.39), but Keller's second goal at 19:32 sealed the 4-2 final.

Strip out the special teams and the game was close: at even strength the expected goals were 1.84 for UTA and 1.70 for EDM, and the shot attempts were 56 to 58. The overall edge, 3.16 to 2.09, still gave UTA a 68% chance of winning a replay. Goaltending was a wash, with Karel Vejmelka and Levi both within about a tenth of a goal of expectation. Keller finished with two goals and Cooley a goal and an assist.
